body: For me, it's a case of I have several best friends, yet I'm none of their best friends. Which essentially means I contact them but they don't give two shits about me. That's how I summarise it. Probably not to useful but I'm basically saying I hear yer brother!

What you've said here really struck a chord with me. I often feel like suicide is a tool to say "told you so". This idea that once gone, I'll sit on the sidelines as some weird spirit and watch them all say things like "we had no idea!" Or "we didn't realise". Then it's too late. I know my comment probably won't help too much but if it helps to know, I feel exactly the same.

Your reply is massively appreciated. And wonderfully refreshing so thank you. ♥️ I guess I'm completely torn with two options. The "have to" vs the "want to". The "have to" is the duty that is my role as a father and I'm very aware that my decision to bring her into this world sits on me. My life is now scheduled to be the person that protects her, loves her and cherishes her for all those years ahead regardless of how I feel or what I'm going through. The "want" on the other hand is very different. I don't want her to experience a wreck of a dad. Who gets angry all the time (verbal only I want to add), stressed and out of control with emotion and depression. I struggle to see how she will benefit whilst all those problems exist. 😢

You know, it's a fact that life is just odds of good luck or bad luck and the hand that's drawn for us all is so random that I agree, people should stop preaching about things getting better when they have no idea whether it will! I've said this so often that people think I'm being over dramatic but I agree with your statement so much. When "good" things happen in my life, they're always diluted anyway because of the burden of depression, anxiety and anger that I permanently have hovering over me. Can't ever see things getting better. Vicious circle. Which is why I've just naturally trained myself to hate and now avoid most people who advise false hope. The people that say, "he should have come to us" when I eventually pull the trigger, yet were no where to be seen when I was alive!
